segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the final scope for the rollout before I send the order form. I have 42 seats for the operations team, start date September 1, and the standard implementation package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. The only thing is we may add 6 more users in October if the Dallas team comes on, but I don't want those on the initial invoice.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, that works. We'll write the order for 42 seats now, and any additional seats can be added later at the same per-seat rate through the co-term process.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the annual total you sent was $31,920, correct?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. That's $760 per seat annually, so $31,920 for the subscription. Implementation is a one-time $4,500, so first-year total is $36,420 before applicable tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Got it. Our finance team asked if the invoice can show the implementation fee as a separate line item.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, no problem. I'll note that in the billing tool and on the order form. It'll show subscription and implementation separately.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Contract term is 12 months, not auto-renewing for multiple years, right?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, 12-month initial term. It does auto-renew for another 12 months unless either side gives 30 days' notice. That's our standard language.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that's fine. If you send it today, I can route it for signature tomorrow morning.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. I'll send the order form by 3 p.m. Eastern, with the September 1 go-live and the invoice note included. Once it's signed, our implementation coordinator will reach out within one business day.
